data.name: Barak
data.gender_notes: Barak is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Barak is a Hebrew name meaning 'lightning' or 'son of light'. In the Old Testament, Barak is the name of a hero who led the Israelites in battle against the Canaanites. When God spoke to Barak, He said, 'Go, take position at Mount Tabor. I will call to Sisera, the captain of Jabin's army, to the River Kishon. Then march against him, and I will give him and his army into your hand.' (Judges 4:6-7). Barak obeyed God's command and led the Israelites to a great victory.
data.spiritual_meaning: Barak represents the power of God and the courage and obedience of those who trust in Him.
data.etymology: Barak belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Son of Light.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Barak total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_english.name: Barak
in_english.meaning: son of thunder, messenger, or voice of the Lord
in_english.long_meaning: son of thunder, messenger, or voice of the Lord, originating from the Hebrew root 'barak', meaning to bless or kneel. In the Christian tradition, the name Barak is associated with the biblical figure of Barak, a judge of Israel who led the Israelites to victory against the Canaanites. The name is also linked to the Greek word 'barakos', meaning thunderbolt. As a given name, Barak conveys strength, courage, and a strong connection to one's faith.

data.cultural_impact: Barak's name in history represents bravery and leadership. He is a hero who led his people to victory in a time of war. The name Barak has been passed down through generations, inspiring those with the name to embody the qualities of this ancient hero.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Barak holds a deeper spiritual significance as it is a reminder of God's faithfulness and power. When God called upon Barak to lead his people, He assured Him of victory before the battle even began. Barak's obedience and trust in God's promise led to a great victory for the Israelites. This story not only encourages us to trust in God's promises but also to be bold and obedient in the face of adversity.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Barak, meaning "lightning" or "thunder" in Hebrew, symbolizes divine power and strength, reminding us of God's ability to strike with swift and decisive action against injustice and adversity. It also represents the courage and determination one needs to follow God's call to lead and conquer, just as Barak, a biblical hero, did in conquering the Canaanites at the battle of Mount Tabor.

biblical_reference.note: Barak is a judge of Israel who led the Israelites to victory against the Canaanites with the help of Deborah, a prophetess

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Judge Barak is the second judge in the book of Judges in the Hebrew Bible. The name Barak carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Barak is a military leader who leads the Israelites to victory against the Canaanites.
